case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 22-3-2007 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.4419 of 2004)
full_judgment:
Md Nuruzzaman, J: This Civil Appeal, by leave, has arisen out of the judgment and order dated 22-3-2007 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.4419 of 2004 making the Rule absolute and thereby reversing the judgment and decree dated 23-6-2004 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Additional Court, Narayangonj in Title Appeal No.110 of 2002 affirming the judgment and decree dated 15-5-2002 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Rupgonj, Narayangonj in Title Suit No.138 of 1999 decreeing the suit. 

2. Facts, leading to filing of this civil appeal, in short, are that the appellant, as plaintiff, instituted the Title Suit No.138 of 1999 for declaration of his title in the suit land and also for declaration that the judgment and decree dated 28-4-1999 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Rupgonj, Narayangonj, in Title Suit No.58 of 1998, being obtained fraudulently, is illegal and not binding upon him, on the averments that the proforma respondent No.5, on receiving consideration of Taka 10,000, by registered kabala No.4586 dated 12-5-1998 sold in his favour 0.03 acres of land from Plot No.331, 0.03 acres of land from Plot No.330 and 0.011/2 acres of land from Plot No.535, totaling an area of 0.071/2 acres. the proforma respondent No.6, on receiving consideration money of Taka 10,000, by registered Kabala No.4585 on 12-5-1998 sold to him 0.0114 acres from Plot No.331, 0.01½ acres from Plot No.330, 0.01½ acres from Plot No.567, 0.01½ acres from Plot No.566 and non suited 0.01½ acres from Plot No.553, totaling an area of 0.07½, acres, at the time of the above transfers the profoima respondent Nos.5 and 6 also delivered possession of the suit land in his favour. Thereafter the respondent Nos.1-4, in collusion with the proforma respondent Nos.5 and 6, created an anti-dated agreement for sale dated 30-9-1997 showing payment of consideration of Taka 2000 and on the basis of the same claimed that they have purchased the suit land by kabala executed on 20-5-1998 and that after preparation of the above kabala dated 20-5-1998 the deed writer failed to read out the contents of those kabalas to the proforma respondent Nos.5 and 6 and that is why they refused to register the same and left the SR Office on that day. The respondent Nos.1-4 instituted Title Suit No.58 of 1998 in the Court and by practicing fraud upon the Court obtained judgment and decree dated 28-4-1999. The plaintiff, on 22-8-1999, obtaining the certified copy of the judgment came to know about the said decree which clouded his title in the suit land. 

3. The defendant Nos.1-4 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that the proforma respondent Nos.5 and 6 decided to sell the suit land to them at a consideration of Taka 25,000 and accordingly on receiving Taka 10,000 from them the proforma respondent Nos.5 and 6 executed a bainanama on 30-9-1997 in their favour wherein it was stipulated that within 2 years after receiving the balance consideration of Taka 15,000 the proforma respondent Nos.5 and 6 would execute and register the kabala. On 20-5-1998, the respondent Nos.1-4 paid the rest consideration of Taka 15,000 to the proforma respondent Nos.5 and 6 and thereafter, they executed the kabala but due to the delay of presentation of the kabala the same could not be registered on that day. It was then decided that on the next day the proforma respondent Nos.5 and 6 would register the kabala but on the next date the proforma respondent Nos.5 and 6 did not turn up in the office of the sub-Registrar. Thereafter, in spite of repeated requests, the proforma respondent Nos.5 and 6 did not register the sale deed and hence, the respondent Nos.l-4 instituted the above Title suit No.58 of 1998 for specific Performance of Contract. Although notices were duly served upon the proforma respondent Nos.5 and 6, they failed to appear and contest the suit and accordingly the said suit was decreed ex-parte. The appellant, in order to grab the suit and some other lands, by way of false personation created 2 kabala deeds dated 12-5-1998 showing the proforma respondent Nos.5 and 6 as executants and as the bainanama in favour of the respondent Nos.1-4 being earlier on point of time they, on the basis of the same, acquired valid title in the suit land and, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

4. On conclusion of the trial, the learned Assistant Judge, Rupganj, Narayanganj considering the evidences and docuinents on record, decreed the suit by his judgment and decree dated 15-5-2002. 

5. Feeling aggrieved, by the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the defendants as appellants preferred Title Appeal No.110 of 2002 before the District Judge, Narayanganj. On transfer, the said appeal was heard by the learned Joint District Judge, Additional Court, Narayangonj, who by his judgment and decree dated 23-6-2004 disallowed the appeal and thereby affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial Court. 

6. Feeling aggrieved, by the judgment and decree dated 23-6-2004 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Additional Court, Narayanganj, the defendant-appellant-petitioners preferred Civil Revision No.4419 of 2004 before the High Court Division and obtained the Rule. 

7. In due course, a Single Bench of the High Court Division upon hearing the parties made the Rule absolute by the impugned judgment and order dated 22-3-2007 and thereby set-aside the judgment and decree dated 23-6-2004 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Narayangonj, in Title Appeal No.110 of 2002 and the judgment and decree dated 15-5-2002 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Rupganj, in Title Suit No.138 of 1999. 

8. The plaintiff-appellant feeling aggrieved by the impugned judgment and order dated 22-3-2007 of the High Court Division preferred Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.921 of 2007 before this Division and obtained leave, which, gave rise to the instant appeal. 

9. Mr Taufique Anwar Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant submits that the kabala deeds of the plaintiff have been executed and registered on 12-5-1998 and the kabala deed of the defendant-respondent Nos.1-4 has been merely executed on 20-5-1998, moreso was not registered. On the basis of the above kabala deeds dated 12-5-1998 which were earlier in point of time, the plaintiff acquired valid title and after considering the evidence on record the trial Court and appellate Court found that the plaintiff is in possession of the suit land but the High Court Division committed serious illegality in making the Rule absolute. He further submits that in the trial Court and appellate Court found that the defendants failed to prove the Bainapatra and considered it as collusive and illegal but the High Court Division upon misreading and misconstruing the findings of the trial Court and appellate Court below committed an error of law in making the. Rule absolute. He next submits that the kabalas executed in favour of the defendants in pursuance of the decree as passed in Title Suit No.58 of 1998 was a suit for specific performance of contract is subsequent to that of the kabalas dated 12-5-1998 and, as such, the defendants did not acquire any valid right, title and interest in the suit land but the High Court Division committed an error of law in making the Rule absolute. He finally submits that since both the Court of facts, on consideration of the evidence on record, found the possession of the appellant in the suit land, so the respondent Nos.1-4 will not get any benefit of the provision of section 53A of the Transfer of Property Act but the High Court Division committed serious illegality in making the Rule absolute and, as such, the impugned judgment of the High Court Division is liable to be set-aside. 

10. Per contra, Mr Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, the learned Senior Counsel appearing on behalf of the respondents submit that the High Court Division considering the evidences and the materials on record rightly held that the trial Court without considering the exhibits, depositions of the PWs and DWs, plaint, written statements wrongly and illegally decreed the suit and the Appellate Court below also without considering the exhibits, depositions of the PWs and DWs, plaint and written statements dismissed the appeal and affirmed the judgment and decree dated 12-5-2002 passed by the trial Court illegally and, as such, the High Court Division made the Rule absolute and set-aside the judgment and decree passed by the Courts below and, as such, no interference by this Division for ends of justice. He further submits that the High Court Division in exercising his power under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure has held and found that the findings of the Appellate Court below are not just and sustainable in law and since there is merit in the revision, it must succeed, the plaintiff failed to prove his case. He finally submits that the High Court Division elaborately discussed the evidence 
of the PWs and DWs independently and considering the facts and circumstances of the case made the Rule absolute without any order as to cost and the impugned judgment and decree dated 23-6-2004 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Narayanganj in Title Appeal No.110 of 2002 and judgment and decree dated 15-5-2002 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Rupganj, Narayanganj in Title Suit No.138 of 1999 have been set-aside and the suit filed by the plaintiff has been dismissed by the judgment and order dated 22-3-2007 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.4419 of 2004 which requires no interference by this Division for ends of justice. 

11. We have heard the learned Advocates for the respective, parties. Perused the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division and other connected materials on record. 

12. Having gone through the judgment of the High Court Division it transpires that in the impugned judgment the learned Single Judge opined that both the trial Court and the Court of appeal below committed error of law in non-considering the evidences on records both oral and documentary resulting in error in the decision occasioning failure of justice but did not rebut the findings, discussions and opinions of the Courts below as both Courts of facts concurrently after discussing the testimonies of DW 1 to 3 found that the bainapatra was not proved by the proper and competent witnesses. 

13. The defendants adduced 3 witnesses to prove the unregistered deed claiming that it was executed by the defendant Nos.5 and 6. So, this Division has to answer whether execution of the unregistered deed was proved in accordance with law and both Courts below misread and misconstrued the evidences on records. 

14. From the judgments of the Courts below it is crystal clear that both Courts below discussed and appreciated the testimonies of PWs and DWs in its true perspective and came to definite findings that the defendants appellants respondents have failed to prove the genuineness of the unregistered deed with its execution. The Courts below founds that the defendant Nos.5 and 6 did not turn up in Court to support the execution, the scribe and husband of the executant name Shainsun Nahar were not adduced as witnesses in the Court, though DW No.1 admitted that they were present at the time of bainapatra and execution. In cross he admitted that he could not bring the arbitrators as witnesses those were present in Arbitration, admitted that there is no witness in the baina and deed of this village. Further admitted that Mokbul Hossain, a witness to the Bainapatra is his maternal uncle, however, he did not turn up to prove the Bainapatra, he comes from village Jatra Mura far from 3½/4 kilometers from the Borpa i.e. from the suit place. DW 2 is the maternal uncle of the DW 1. DW 2 in examination-in-cross admitted that he did not receive the Court witness notice albeit; he was present and disposed in Court. DW 3 could not tell the correct plot numbers and quantum of the land. He admitted that he was not present at the time of execution of bainapatra and deed in question. 

15. However, in the pliant 4 persons are the plaintiffs, except one as DW No.1, none of the plaintiffs were appeared and deposed in the Court in support of their plaint case in the suit for Specific Performance of Contract as DWs, as both suits were tried analogously by the same Court. 

16. The DW 1 while deposed on behalf of other plaintiffs, he did not produce any supporting documents i.e. Power of Attorney or Letter of authority to prove that he is a competent witness on behalf of other plaintiffs as required under Rules 1 and 2 of Order III of the Code of Civil Procedure. Thus, it may conveniently be noted the provisions of the same in this context. 
Rule 1 runs thus:-
Any appearance, application or act in or to any Court, required or authorized by law to be made or done by a party in shall Court, 
may, except where otherwise expressly provided by any law for the time being in force, be made or done by the party in person, or by his recognized agent, or by a pleaded appearing, applying or acting, as the case may be, on his behalf: 
Provided that any such appearance shall, if the Court so directs, be made by the party in person. 
Rule 2 runs thus:—
The recognized agents of parties by whom such Recognized appearance, applications and acts may be made or done are—
(a) Persons holding powers-of-attorney, authorizing them to make and do such appearances, applications and acts on behalf of such parties; 
(b) Persons carrying on trade or business for and in the names of parties not resident within the local limits of the jurisdiction of the Court within which limits the appearance, application or act is made or done, in matters connected with such trade or business only, where no other agent is expressly authorized to make and do such appearances, applications and acts. 

17. On a breviary of the above provisions of law it is clearly panoramic that a person if not authorise by the plaintiff or defendent, except husband and wife, could not depose on his behalf in the Court, if depose, he would be treated as incompetent witness. The DW No.1 deposed on behalf of other plaintiffs without any authority from them as found from record. Thus, it is obviously proved that he was an un-authorized and incompetent witness to prove the case on behalf of other plaintiffs. 

18. It is the cardinal principle of law as enunciated by this Division that revision Court cannot interfere in concurrent finding of facts, when there is no misreading and non-consideration of the material evidence on records. In the instant case the Single Judge of the High Court Division in the judgment wrongly opined that both the Courts misread and non-considered the materials evidence on record or rebutted the facts of finding of the Courts below as both the Courts below correctly found that the case of the defendant for the Specific Performance of Contract was not proved. 

19. We are, therefore, of the view that the judgment of the High Court Division is not a proper judgment of reversal, thus, it cannot be sustained in law, because, the Court of revision when acts beyond its jurisdiction in setting aside the concurrent findings of fact, this Division obviously interfere in the judgment of the High Court Division to secure the ends of justice. 

20. In the present case, at the time of trial two suits were tried analogously, one suit was for declaration of title and cancellation of ex-parte decree; another was for the Specific Performance of Contract. Both the Courts below concurrently found that suit for declaration and cancellation was proved but suit for Specific Performance of Contract was not proved. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division while reversed the judgments did not even discuss the case on the basis of evidence on record nor opined that the plaintiffs of the suit for Specific Performance of Contract was able to satisfy that the execution of bainapatra and deed were proved, consideration was passed and transaction was found genuine, even if, reversed the concurrent findings of fact which calls for interference by this Division. 

21. The discussions made herein above and the material on records, we are of the view that the judgment of the High Court Division is not a proper judgment of reversal, hence, it is set-aside. The judgment of the Court of appeal below is affirmed. 

Accordingly, this Civil Appeal is allowed, however, without any order as to cost. 

End.
